# `handle_not_sendable`: a resource handle in a message to another node

A resource handle (`File.Handle`, `File.Dir`, `Socket`, `Listener`, `Process`,
`UdpSocket`, `TlsConn`, `TlsCtx`, `WsSocket`) names an open file, socket or
process of THIS node. This error reports a message type that holds one, at any
depth: at its `derive Json`, at a `Node.send` or `Node.enqueue`, or at an
`@[remote]` handler that receives it.

## A program that triggers it

```march
-- EXPECT-ERROR: `Socket` cannot be sent to another node: a handle names a resource on this node
-- ocap phase 2b (Task 13): a resource handle (`File.Handle`, `File.Dir`,
-- `Socket`, `Listener`, `Process`, `UdpSocket`, `TlsConn`, `TlsCtx`,
-- `WsSocket`) is a box over a descriptor of THIS node's process. Encoded and
-- sent anywhere else it would name nothing, or whatever descriptor has that
-- number there, so a message type holding one at any depth is refused at
-- compile time, naming the handle type, instead of the confusing "no JSON
-- codec" a generated encoder used to produce.
mod HandleSend do
  needs IO.NetConnect
  needs IO.Mut

  type Relay = { sock : Socket, n : Int }
  derive Json for Relay

  fn forward(peer : Peer, s : Socket) do
    let r : Relay = { sock: s, n: 1 }
    Node.send(peer, GlobalPid.make("b", 1, 1), r)
  end

  fn main(_n : Cap(IO.NetConnect), _m : Cap(IO.Mut)) do
    ()
  end
end
```

## The fix

Keep the handle on this node and send what the other node needs instead: a
path, an address, or the `GlobalPid.Pid` of an actor here that owns the
resource and answers for it.

```march
mod HandleSend do
  needs IO.NetConnect
  needs IO.Mut

  type Relay = { addr : String, n : Int }
  derive Json for Relay

  fn forward(peer : Peer, addr : String) do
    let r : Relay = { addr: addr, n: 1 }
    Node.send(peer, GlobalPid.make("b", 1, 1), r)
  end

  fn main(_n : Cap(IO.NetConnect), _m : Cap(IO.Mut)) do
    ()
  end
end
```

## Why the rule exists

A handle is a box over a descriptor of the sending process. Decoded on another
node it would name nothing, or whatever descriptor has the same number there,
so no codec over a handle is generated, and a send of one is refused at compile
time rather than failing, or misdirecting, at run time.

See also: [the language reference](../clustering.md).
